paper.title_en: Probing axion-induced X-ray emission in magnetic white dwarfs
paper.abstract_en: Magnetic white dwarfs are dense celestial objects with strong magnetic fields that lie in the range of <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>9</mn></msup><mi>G</mi></mrow></math>. Axions are produced in their stellar core by axion bremsstrahlung in electron-ion scattering, and these axions are converted to X-ray photons in the magnetosphere of a magnetic white dwarf. Here we study the conversion to a photon by the Primakoff effect. Our findings explore X-ray luminosity of the order of 10<sup loc="post">14</sup>erg/s for the axion mass in μeV, providing a quantitative estimate of the axion-induced X-ray emission from magnetic white dwarfs. We computed the X-ray luminosity of some magnetic white dwarfs(WD 1533-057, WD 1017+367, WD 1043-050) as a function of axion mass.
